items.title: File Martin County business personal property return
items.description: Martin County provides the DR-405 tangible personal property return and requires annual reporting to the Property Appraiser by April 1; the county also identifies a $25,000 business TPP exemption.

note: Martin County collects its own tourist development tax (5%, per Florida's DR-15TDT), but no official county page with the registration steps and due date could be read.

items.title: File Miami-Dade County business personal property return
items.description: Florida tangible personal property tax returns (Form DR-405) are due to the county property appraiser by April 1, even if the business owes nothing, to claim the exemption. The return goes to the county property appraiser.

items.title: Register for the Miami-Dade County tourist development tax
items.description: Operators of hotels, motels and short-term rentals (stays of six months or less) register with the county to collect the 6% (7% in Miami Beach; 4% in Surfside and Bal Harbour) tourist development tax. Florida's Department of Revenue lists Miami-Dade as a county that collects it directly rather than through the state sales tax return; the state sales tax on the same rentals is still filed on the DR-15 (line D).

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Miami-Dade County tourist development tax return
items.description: The county's convention and tourist tax return is monthly, due on the 1st and late if not received by the 20th of the following month (next business day if that is a weekend or holiday), even with no tax collected. Non-electronic filing costs $10 per filing and payment since October 2025.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: Obtain or renew the Miami-Dade County business tax receipt
items.description: Miami-Dade County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. Florida law makes the receipt payable by September 30 (late penalty 10% for October, then 5% more each month, up to 25%). The tax year runs October 1 to September 30. Apply and renew online through BTExpress; fees depend on business type and location. Businesses inside a city generally need both a city and a county receipt. Applicants must attest they do not do business with Cuba in violation of federal law (Florida Statutes 205.0532).

items.title: File Monroe County business personal property return
items.description: Monroe County provides the DR-405 tangible personal property return through the Property Appraiser; Florida requires the annual return by April 1, with timely filing needed to preserve the $25,000 exemption.

note: Monroe County collects its own tourist development tax (5%, per Florida's DR-15TDT), but no official county page with the registration steps and due date could be read.

items.title: File Nassau County business personal property return
items.description: Columbia County Property Appraiser requires anyone possessing taxable assets on January 1 to file the DR-405 tangible personal property return by April 1; the county publishes April 1 as the filing deadline.

items.title: Register for the Nassau County tourist development tax
items.description: Operators of hotels, motels and short-term rentals (stays of six months or less) register with the county to collect the 5% (Amelia Island, ZIP 32034) tourist development tax. Florida's Department of Revenue lists Nassau as a county that collects it directly rather than through the state sales tax return; the state sales tax on the same rentals is still filed on the DR-15 (line D).

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Nassau County tourist development tax return
items.description: The county's return form (2018 revision, the latest found) says to file and pay by the 20th of each month after collection. The late penalty is 10% per 30 days up to 50%, minimum $50.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Okaloosa County business personal property return
items.description: Okaloosa County requires tangible personal property to be reported annually to the Property Appraiser on DR-405; returns and extension requests are due by April 1, and failure to file does not remove the obligation or penalties.

items.title: Register for the Okaloosa County tourist development tax
items.description: Operators of hotels, motels and short-term rentals (stays of six months or less) register with the county to collect the 6% tourist development tax. Florida's Department of Revenue lists Okaloosa as a county that collects it directly rather than through the state sales tax return; the state sales tax on the same rentals is still filed on the DR-15 (line D).

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Okaloosa County tourist development tax return
items.description: Since January 1, 2022 the Clerk, not the state, collects the tax. Returns are monthly through the Clerk's online portal, due the 1st and penalized if not filed and paid by the 20th (an older FAQ says postmarked by the 20th). The penalty is 10% or $50, whichever is greater.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Okeechobee County business personal property return
items.description: Okeechobee County requires anyone with taxable business assets on January 1 to file a DR-405 with the Property Appraiser by April 1; the county warns that nonfiling can result in a 25% penalty.

note: Florida's DR-15TDT lists Okeechobee County's tourist development tax as collected by the Department of Revenue, so lodging operators report it on the state sales tax return (DR-15), not to the county.

items.title: File Orange County business personal property return
items.description: Orange County provides online, email, and mail filing for the DR-405 tangible personal property return; Florida requires the return by April 1 each year to the county Property Appraiser.

items.title: Register for the Orange County tourist development tax

Florida's Department of Revenue lists Orange as a county that collects it directly rather than through the state sales tax return; the state sales tax on the same rentals is still filed on the DR-15 (line D).

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Orange County tourist development tax return
items.description: The Comptroller administers the tax. It is remitted monthly, due on the 1st of the month after collection and delinquent if not postmarked by the 20th. Online filing is available.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: Obtain or renew the Orange County business tax receipt
items.description: Orange County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. Florida law makes the receipt payable by September 30 (late penalty 10% for October, then 5% more each month, up to 25%). Renewal notices are mailed before expiration; renew by mail, in person or online. Businesses in a city such as Orlando or Maitland must hold that city's receipt before applying for the county receipt.

items.title: File Osceola County business personal property return
items.description: Osceola County directs property owners to its Property Appraiser for tangible personal property records and filing; the annual DR-405 return is due by April 1 under Florida law.

items.title: Register for the Osceola County tourist development tax

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Osceola County tourist development tax return
items.description: Returns postmarked after the 20th of the month due incur a penalty of 10% of the tax or $50, whichever is greater; returns postmarked by the 20th may keep a 2.5% collection allowance (maximum $30). The county does not contract with Airbnb, VRBO or similar platforms to collect for owners.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: Obtain or renew the Osceola County business tax receipt
items.description: Osceola County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. Existing receipts renew annually for $30.00 from July 1, per the Tax Collector's page.

items.title: File Palm Beach County business personal property return
items.description: Florida tangible personal property tax returns (Form DR-405) are due to the county property appraiser by April 1, even if the business owes nothing, to claim the exemption. Returns can be filed through the county's online TPP system.

items.title: Register for the Palm Beach County tourist development tax
items.description: Operators of hotels, motels and short-term rentals (stays of six months or less) register with the county to collect the 6% tourist development tax. appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Palm Beach County tourist development tax return
items.description: Monthly reporting is due on the 1st and late after the 20th, with interest and penalties. Online platforms do not remit to the Tax Collector for hosts.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: Obtain or renew the Palm Beach County business tax receipt
items.description: Palm Beach County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. items.title: File Pasco County business personal property return

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.description: Pasco County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. Some cities require the county receipt before issuing the city receipt.

items.title: File Pinellas County business personal property return

items.title: File the Pinellas County tourist development tax return
items.description: Returns are monthly and delinquent unless filed and paid by the 20th of the month following collection, even if no rental activity. The late penalty is 10% with a $50 minimum, plus interest.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Polk County business personal property return
items.description: Florida tangible personal property tax returns (Form DR-405) are due to the county property appraiser by April 1, even if the business owes nothing, to claim the exemption. Late filing carries 5% per month, capped at 25%.

items.description: Operators of hotels, motels and short-term rentals (stays of six months or less) register with the county to collect the 5% tourist development tax. appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Polk County tourist development tax return
items.description: Remittances are due on the 1st of the month after collection and are delinquent if not paid by the 20th. From August 17, 2026 monthly filings must be entered in the Phenix online system. The Tax Collector may approve quarterly, semiannual or annual filing for accounts that meet its criteria.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: Obtain or renew the Polk County business tax receipt
items.description: Polk County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. Florida law makes the receipt payable by September 30 (late penalty 10% for October, then 5% more each month, up to 25%). Pay online or by mail postmarked before October 1. From October 1 a 10% penalty plus collection costs applies, and the penalty grows each month through March.

items.title: File Putnam County business personal property return
items.description: Putnam County requires owners, lessees, or custodians of tangible personal property to file a DR-405 with the Property Appraiser; timely filing is required for the exemption and late filing can cause a penalty of up to 25%.

note: Putnam County collects its own tourist development tax (4%, per Florida's DR-15TDT), but no official county page with the registration steps and due date could be read.

items.title: File Santa Rosa County business personal property return

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Sarasota County business personal property return

items.title: File Seminole County business personal property return
items.description: Seminole County provides a Property Appraiser TPP e-file portal for the DR-405 return; Florida requires the annual return to be filed with the county Property Appraiser by April 1.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Seminole County tourist development tax return
items.description: Due by the 20th of the month after collection; a postmark of the 21st or later adds interest and penalties. Independent rentals also need a Business Tax Receipt from the Tax Collector. Airbnb, VRBO and similar platforms collect for hosts who use them.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.description: Seminole County issues a business tax receipt through its Tax Collector. Florida law makes the receipt payable by September 30 (late penalty 10% for October, then 5% more each month, up to 25%). The fee is $25 for a non-regulated business and $45 for a regulated one. Businesses in unincorporated Seminole County need only the county receipt. A fine of $250 may be added to a receipt not obtained or renewed within 150 days of notice.

items.title: File St. Johns County business personal property return
items.description: St. Johns County requires business owners and self-employed contractors with tangible personal property on January 1 to file the DR-405 return with the Property Appraiser each year; the county assesses all TPP in the county.

items.title: Register for the St. Johns County tourist development tax

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the St. Johns County tourist development tax return
items.description: Due on the 1st of the month after collection and delinquent if not postmarked by the 20th. A return is required every month even when no tax is due. Registering needs a Florida sales tax number, a St. Johns County Business Tax Receipt and the county's tourist development tax application.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File St. Lucie County business personal property return

items.description: Sumter County requires owners of business tangible personal property on January 1 to report it annually to the Property Appraiser; DR-405 returns are due by April 1, and extensions must be requested before the deadline.

note: Florida's DR-15TDT lists no tourist development tax for Sumter County (0%).

items.title: File Suwannee County business personal property return
items.description: Suwannee County requires businesses to file the DR-405 tangible personal property return with the Property Appraiser by April 1 each year; the county provides the form and filing instructions.

items.title: File the Taylor County tourist development tax return
items.description: Remitted monthly, due the 1st of the month after collection and delinquent if not paid or postmarked by the 20th.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Union County business personal property return
items.description: Union County requires anyone possessing taxable assets on January 1 to file a DR-405 tangible personal property return with the Property Appraiser each year; Florida law requires annual reporting.

note: Florida's DR-15TDT lists no tourist development tax for Union County (0%).

items.title: File Volusia County business personal property return
items.description: Volusia County requires owners of tangible personal property used in business to file the county VC-405 return with the Property Appraiser each year; timely filing supports the county's $25,000 exemption.

items.title: Register for the Volusia County tourist development tax

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.description: Wakulla County requires anyone owning tangible personal property on January 1 to file the DR-405 return with the Property Appraiser by April 1 each year unless the county has waived the filing requirement.

note: Florida's DR-15TDT lists Wakulla County's tourist development tax as collected by the Department of Revenue, so lodging operators report it on the state sales tax return (DR-15), not to the county.

items.title: File Walton County business personal property return
items.description: Walton County's Property Appraiser provides tangible property search and DR-405 forms; Florida requires business tangible personal property returns to be filed with the county by April 1.

items.title: Register for the Walton County tourist development tax
items.description: Operators of hotels, motels and short-term rentals (stays of six months or less) register with the county to collect the 5% (2% in parts of the county; the county says 3% north of Choctawhatchee Bay) tourist development tax. items.title: File the Walton County tourist development tax return
items.description: Returns are due by the 20th of the month following the stay, including months with no bookings. Register and file through the county's GovOS online portal.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Washington County business personal property return
items.description: Washington County's Tax Collector collects tangible personal property tax after the Property Appraiser assesses the roll; taxes become delinquent April 1, while property-roll changes are handled by the Property Appraiser.

note: Florida's DR-15TDT lists Washington County's tourist development tax as collected by the Department of Revenue, so lodging operators report it on the state sales tax return (DR-15), not to the county.
